opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Undergraduate Tuition Fee Grants

amount.raw: grants cover the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Individuals from low-income households who are ineligible for tuition fee support from the Scottish Government; ordinarily resident in Scotland; enrolled on or holding an unconditional offer for an undergraduate degree course at an eligible Scottish Higher Education Institution; not already graduated with a university degree (except for 2nd degree scheme).
opportunities.summary: Covers the cost of tuition fees (up to £1,820/year) for undergraduate students from low-income households studying at an eligible Scottish Higher Education Institution who are not eligible for government funding for their tuition fees. Application portal open 1 June 2026 to 5pm 1 December 2026 for academic year 2026-27.

opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Carnegie-Morgan Scholarship

amount.raw: Full tuition fees for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants plus an additional living-cost bursary of £1,200

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scottish-domiciled students from low-income households, ordinarily resident in Scotland, who have been accepted onto the MSc Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants (delivered by Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh and University of Edinburgh), studying part-time or full-time, and who do not already hold a postgraduate degree.
opportunities.summary: A partnership between Carnegie Education Fund and the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh providing full tuition fees and a £1,200 living-cost bursary for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants, widening participation in postgraduate study in plant science and botany. No stated deadline; applicants apply for the course first and then are directed to CEF for the scholarship.
